status: executed; 10 completed pairs; isolated blind grading; counterbalanced; opaque working directories
trial: v2 frozen packet comparison - leak-free replication
purpose: Re-run the replication after correcting a generation-side working-directory leak found in review: the 2026-09-16 harnesses named each arm's directory after its own arm, and the headless CLI places the working directory in the model's context.
supersedes_note: The 2026-09-16 run's numbers stand as recorded and are not regraded or rewritten. This run is the leak-free instrument and is the one the conclusion should rest on.
surface: Claude Code CLI, headless (-p) on Linux
surface_version_change: The 2026-09-16 runs used CLI 2.1.273; this container had updated to 2.1.274 by 2026-09-17. This is a real difference between the runs, so the two are not a same-condition replication.
provider_note: The CLI result JSON reports a model id but no provider field. Routing is host-managed and not independently verifiable from this run.

leak_correction.defect: Arm working directories were named `pNN-baseline` / `pNN-candidate`, so each generating call could read a word naming its own arm.
leak_correction.verification: Tested 2026-09-17 on CLI 2.1.274: `claude -p` with `--strict-mcp-config --tools ""` in a directory named `.../p01-candidate` returned its own full cwd path verbatim without calling a tool.
leak_correction.fix: Every call now runs in a directory named by a random 6-byte hex token carrying no arm, order or label information. The token is recorded per call as `cwd_token`.
leak_correction.scope: Grader blinding was never affected; grader directories carried only the shuffled A/B label and the mapping was written outside the grader's input.

timeout_note: 300 s chosen per-process budget, not a proven sufficient timeout. No call approached it.

configuration.argv_note: All 40 calls used this exact flag sequence; only <PROMPT> varied. Each call's prompt is identified by prompt_sha256 in this record and is also present verbatim in the committed bundle.json as that call's argv[2], so all 40 digests recompute from committed bytes without reconstruction. Arm prompts are the frozen packet files verbatim; each grader prompt is frozen rubric.md + the harness's fixed isolated-grading instruction + the committed blind output.
configuration.context_isolation: Every call ran in its own empty directory outside the repository, named by an opaque token, so neither project context files nor the directory name could inform the model. User- and global-scope CLI configuration was not isolated. The isolation claimed here is arm-freedom, not absolute context-freedom: every working directory still sits under a scratch path naming this repository and this run. That parent path is identical for both arms, so it cannot bias a paired comparison, but a future claim of absolute isolation would need a neutral parent.
configuration.blinding_note: Execution order is counterbalanced by design (odd pairs baseline-first, even pairs candidate-first). The A/B blind label is an independent per-pair shuffle and is NOT counterbalanced — A is the candidate in 6 of 10 pairs here. That is immaterial under isolated grading, because the label never enters a grader prompt: each prompt is the frozen rubric plus the fixed instruction plus one output, with no pair number, arm or label. The label names a file and nothing else.

paired_difference_candidate_minus_baseli.interval_note: Both intervals are computed from the unrounded standard error (0.089752747); the displayed sd and standard_error are that same quantity rounded for reading. Multiplying the rounded SE instead would move a z bound by 9.262e-05 and a t bound by 0.0001069 — the shift scales with the critical value, so it is not one number for both intervals. These are measured on the unrounded bounds; differencing the rounded bounds would only ever report a multiple of 1e-4. The t critical value 2.262 is the two-sided 95% value for df=9, derived from this input rather than fixed.

findings: No advantage demonstrated, on a leak-free instrument. The paired difference is -0.05 points out of 4, spanning zero on both a normal interval [-0.2259, +0.1259] and a t(9) interval [-0.2530, +0.1530]. Seven of ten pairs tied, two favoured the baseline and one favoured the candidate.

The working-directory leak did not produce the earlier result. Removing it left the null intact and tightened it: ties rose from 5/10 to 7/10 and the paired sd fell from 0.369 to 0.284. The difference changed sign, from +0.05 to -0.05, which is what variation around zero looks like rather than a treatment effect in either direction.

Rubric saturation reproduces independently. Checks 1, 2 and 3 again scored 1.0 for both arms in all twenty gradings. Only check 4 moves (baseline 0.90, candidate 0.85), and it moves within each arm. Two independent runs now show the instrument has effectively one discriminating check.
conclusion: The 2026-09-16 conclusion survives correction: on this frozen synthetic packet the structured handoff presentation shows no measurable advantage over the prose session note, and no promotion claim follows. The saturation finding is now the more durable result of the two, having reproduced on a leak-free instrument and a different CLI build.
limitations: One synthetic transferred packet on one scenario. This does not test filesystem discovery, real repository artifacts, actual task execution or cross-agent portability.
The graders are separate processes but the same vendor and model family as the arms; none is an independent or human reviewer.
Each grader call scores one output in isolation, but all graders share a model; a systematic grader bias would not be detected by repetition.
n=10 gives a coarse variance estimate on a three-valued score scale. Both intervals are indicative, not formal significance tests.
Because checks 1-3 are saturated, a null here is weak evidence of equivalence rather than proof of it.
Token counts and costs are the CLI's own reported figures; they are not a billing measurement.
All calls ran on claude-sonnet-5 under CLI 2.1.274 on Linux. Nothing generalises to another surface, model or version, and the CLI build differs from the 2026-09-16 runs.
relation_to_prior_records: Additive in its measurements; the frozen packet bytes, the v1 attempt and the 2026-09-06 reviewer-reported pair are untouched, and no prior run is regraded. derivation.note: harness.py executes the trial and writes bundle.json; it computes no statistics. The aggregate block was originally derived by an uncommitted step, which is how a rounding defect reached this record: that step rounded sd before deriving the standard error and then multiplied the rounded SE. The size of that shift is not restated here: it is measured per interval by the producer and reported in aggregate.paired_difference_candidate_minus_baseline.rounded_se_bound_shift, because it scales with the critical value and a second hand-written copy is a second thing to drift. An earlier description of this record blamed a helper inside harness.py; that is withdrawn, since harness.py contains no such code. The producer is now committed alongside its input and recorded in evidence_file_sha256, so the derivation is reproducible and not merely recomputable.
